notes: before this record. The announcement thread and the live site disagree on storage: 60 MB in the 2026-05-21 LET post, 150 MB on the rules page last updated 2026-05-24. The live page is the one a new applicant is provisioned from, so the record uses 150 MB and writes the disagreement down. What could not be established: the traffic allowance, and whether the IRC admin gate is answered promptly (the thread shows signups accepted the day after the announcement, so the gate does clear). The 90-day clock resets on a dashboard login as well as SSH, which makes it cheaper to hold than serv00's SSH-only clock.

free_tier.stated: Batch 1 recorded shellter.me as a free bash account on a shared FreeBSD host: 150 MB of ZFS home, three IPv6 addresses and a 50-port TCP slot, accepted manually on IRC. The operator's own rules page states the enforcement plainly, quoted: 'We can suspend or terminate any account at any time, with or without notice, with or without prior warning.' A user in the launch thread reports the enforcement working on a working account within a day, quoted: 'Your shell account [username] has been suspended. Active sessions were terminated and new logins are blocked.' The operator replied: 'you was flagged and suspended by our automatic anti abuse system.'

superseded.notes: The spec is small and batch 1 had it right. The finding is the enforcement shape: the account was suspended within a day of being provisioned, and the trigger was the operator's automatic system reading something in the user's session, not a published quota. The same thread shows the recovery path works, because the operator answered on the forum in the same hour. A reader should conclude that this is a host for interactive work with a person reachable behind it, and not a place for a daemon. Conflicting verdicts across agents: qualifies via b01-boxybsd. The one recorded is the better-evidenced.
